# Background

We have the MNIST data consisting of digitized images of handwritten arabic numerals.

```{r lkdat}
data("mnist", package="glmmlpack260")
str(mnist)
mt8ind = which(mnist$train$labels==8)
imgs8 = mnist$train$images[mt8ind,]
par(mfrow=c(2,2),mar=c(4,3,2,2))
for (i in 1:4) image(matrix(imgs8[i,], 28)[,28:1])
```

Each image has 784 = 28 x 28 intensity values from 0 to 255.  R's
`image` function can help us recognize the variability in
handwritten numerals.

That computers can perform handwriting recognition is well-established.
How do they do it?  We will examine steps towards an answer.

# Feature exploration

The images present a "human readable" view of the data.  One
"feature" of interest is the pattern of intensity along a line 
in the "middle" of the image.

```{r lktra}
par(mfrow=c(2,2),mar=c(4,3,2,2))
for (i in 1:4) {
   image(matrix(imgs8[i,], 28)[,28:1])
   abline(v=.5)
}
```

We can extract the data values corresponding to this
"middle" line and plot the intensities.

```{r lktra2}
par(mfrow=c(2,2),mar=c(4,3,2,2))
for (i in 1:4) {
   plot(matrix(imgs8[i,], 28)[,28:1][14,]) # why?
}
```

The intent here is to identify the "column" of the image
matrix that exhibits three peaks of intensity.

It turns out that the 15th "column" of the image matrix
will exhibit the three peaks characteristic of a vertical
scan of the handwritten "8".  We need the indices into
the 784-column matrix of thousands of numerals that have
been scanned.

```{r lklineinds}
lineinds = which(((matrix(0:783 %% 28, 28))+1)==15) 
imgs8[1:4, lineinds]
```

We propose the 28 features identified in this way as sufficient
to identify an "8".  Surely we can do better, but let's see
if this is a useful setp.

# Exercise 1.

Produce four images for the numeral 1.

```{r lk1}
mt1ind = which(mnist$train$labels==1)
imgs1 = mnist$train$images[mt1ind,]
par(mfrow=c(2,2),mar=c(4,3,2,2))
for (i in 1:4) image(matrix(imgs1[i,], 28)[,28:1])
```
 
Build a tree-structured classifier.

```{r lktr}
newdat = data.frame(num="8", imgs8[, lineinds])
newdat = rbind(newdat, data.frame(num="1", imgs1[, lineinds]))
newdat$num = factor(newdat$num)
library(rpart)
t1 = rpart(num~., data=newdat)
t1
plot(t1)
text(t1)
```
